questions.question: In OR Modelling, networks consist of vertices and edges. Which conditions together define a tree?
options: It is undirected and contains no cycle; it may be split.
It is undirected and connected; cycles are allowed in it.
It is directed, connected, and has no cycle in it at all.
It is undirected and connected, and it contains no cycle.

questions.question: Let $u$ and $v$ be two distinct vertices of a tree. (A path uses distinct edges; a cycle is a closed path.) How many paths join $u$ and $v$?
options: At least two paths, one in each direction between them
Exactly one path, whether or not $u$, $v$ are adjacent
Exactly one path, but only when $u$ and $v$ are adjacent
None at all, unless an edge joins $u$ and $v$ directly

questions.question: An undirected network has vertices A, B, C and edges A–B, B–C and C–A. Is it a tree?
options: No, since A–B–C–A forms a cycle in this network.
Yes, since every vertex is joined to every other.
Yes, since each vertex lies on exactly two edges.
No, since the network is not connected at all.

questions.question: Four vertices A, B, C, D are joined only by the edges A–B and C–D. Does this undirected network form a tree?
options: Yes, since the network contains no cycle at all.
Yes, since each of its two pieces has one edge.
No, since no path joins A to C in this network.
No, since the edges A–B and C–D form a cycle.

questions.question: A tree is to be selected inside a larger undirected network. Which statement about its vertices and edges is correct?
options: It must use every single vertex of the larger network.
It must use every single edge of the larger network.
It uses some of the network's vertices and edges.
It may use edges that the larger network lacks.

questions.question: A tree has 12 vertices. How many edges does it have?
A tree has edges A–B, B–C, B–D, D–E and E–F. How many edges does the path from C to F contain?
A tree has edges P–Q, Q–R, R–S, Q–U and U–V. The edge S–V is added. How many edges does the resulting cycle contain?
An undirected network consists of a single vertex A and no edges. Is it a tree?
options: Yes: it is connected with no cycle and $0$ edges.
No: a tree needs at least one edge to exist.
No: a tree needs at least two separate vertices.
Yes, though it breaks the rule of $n-1$ edges.

questions.question: In a tree, the vertices $u$ and $v$ are not adjacent. (A path uses distinct edges; a cycle is a closed path.) An edge $u$–$v$ is added. Which statement about the new network is correct?
options: It is still a tree, as it is still connected.
It now contains a cycle, so it is not a tree.
It is a tree only when $u$, $v$ are far apart.
It is no longer a tree, as it is disconnected.

questions.question: In a tree, the edge $u$–$v$ is removed. (A path uses distinct edges; a cycle is a closed path.) Which statement about the remaining network is correct?
options: Nothing joins $u$ and $v$ now, so it is disconnected.
It is still connected, via a route avoiding $u$–$v$.
It contains a cycle through $u$ and $v$ instead.
It is disconnected only if $u$ or $v$ lies on one edge.

questions.question: An undirected network has vertices A, B, C, D, E and edges A–B, B–C and D–E. What should be added so that it becomes a tree?
options: The single edge A–C
The single edge B–D
Nothing; it is a tree already
Both edges A–D and C–E

questions.question: An undirected network has edges A–B, B–C, C–A, A–D, D–E and E–F. Removing which edges leaves a tree on all six vertices A to F?
options: Removing the edge A–D
Removing both C–A and A–D
Removing no edge at all
Removing the edge C–A

questions.question: A larger undirected network has 10 vertices and 20 edges. A tree is chosen inside it, using 7 of its vertices and some of its edges. How many edges does this tree have?
A student claims that every undirected network with $n$ vertices and $n-1$ edges is a tree. Which network shows the claim is false?
options: Triangle A–B–C plus a separate vertex D
Path A–B–C–D through all four vertices
Triangle A–B–C with no fourth vertex
Two separate edges A–B and C–D

questions.question: A connected undirected network has $n$ vertices and exactly $n$ edges. (A path uses distinct edges; a cycle is a closed path.) Which statement about it must be true?
options: It may be a tree, as being connected is all that is required.
It must be disconnected, as $n$ edges is one edge too many.
It contains a cycle, since a tree on $n$ vertices has $n-1$ edges.
It contains no cycle, as the edges and vertices are equal in number.

questions.question: An undirected network consists of three separate trees, with 4, 5 and 6 vertices, and no edges between them. How many edges does the network have?
In a tree, the path from A to D is A–B–C–D and the path from A to E is A–B–E. (A path uses distinct edges; a cycle is a closed path.) What is the path from D to E?
options: D–C–B–E
D–C–B–A–B–E
D–E
D–C–E
